newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols mixed ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols mixed ahead of weekend.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were narrowly mixed in late trade after small early gains dissipated under the weight of weekend time decay, dealers said.
With the bond market rebounding after steadily eroding this week from last Friday's four-month highs, interest in downside strike prices appeared to have waned, they added.

"August got bid up a little early, but it's come off and probably will settle a little lower," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. "We don't expect much and we're taking out time decay."
Implied volatility for August T-bond futures options was marginally firmer at around 7.4 percent after blipping up to 7.5 early in the session. September eased 0.1 to about 8.0.

Caution ahead of the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting supported volatilities somewhat. But traders said the meeting was not a very big event-risk as the Federal Reserve was highly unlikely to raise interest rates at this point.
Traders said Thursday's June employment report might bring some excitement, but the long Independence Day weekend immediately following the data dampened interest in options.
Prospects of steady interest rates near term, which have kept the shorter end of the yield curve at a standstill for nearly two weeks, were subduing Eurodollar volatilities.

"The market could always surprise us and move, but it's been a long time," said a Eurodollar trader for a European bank affiliate at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "We've been in a tight trading range for a long time here."
Implied volatilities for December and March Eurodollar futures options were at 9.4 and 11.4 percent, virtually unchanged from late Thursday levels.
